tests: [CDPSession.test] Target.createCDPSession should not report created targets for custom CDP sessions
reason: Creates a CDP session from inside a context's `targetcreated` handler and checks the handler is called once. Strider has no session object to create from a context, and no context target-created event to hang one on; the nearest matrix row is the context's session row

tests: [CDPSession.test] Target.createCDPSession should not send extra events
reason: Listens to every event on a session with `client.on('*')` and checks that only the `Network` domain's events arrive. Strider's session subscriptions are per event, with no listener for all events; the nearest matrix row is the session's event row

tests: [CDPSession.test] Target.createCDPSession should enable and disable domains independently
reason: Strider won't collect coverage from a browser run (ROOK-385, ROOK-386): build-time instrumentation, read back with evaluate, works on every browser. Starts and stops JS coverage (`page.coverage.startJSCoverage` and `stopJSCoverage`) between a session's own `Debugger.enable` and the `scriptParsed` event it waits for. Strider has no JS coverage

tests: [CDPSession.test] Target.createCDPSession should expose the underlying connection
reason: Reads `client.connection()`, the Puppeteer connection object a session belongs to. Strider has no session object; the nearest matrix row is the session's send, which the port covers through the protocol layer

tests: [CDPSession.test] Target.createCDPSession should keep the underlying connection after being detached
reason: Reads `client.connection()` before and after `client.detach()` and checks it is the same object. Strider has no session object to detach or to hold a connection on; the nearest matrix row is the session's detach

Reads `client.detached`, false before and true after `client.detach()`. Strider has no session object with a detached flag; the nearest matrix row is the session's detach, and the port checks the ended session's reason instead

tests: [CDPSession.test] Target.createCDPSession should handle session callbacks when Chrome sends error without sessionId
reason: Builds Puppeteer's own `CdpCDPSession` class and inserts it into the connection's private session map, then checks how the session handles an error Chrome sends without a session id. This tests Puppeteer's internal bookkeeping; Strider's protocol client has no session map to put a session in
